questions_and_answers.question_text: What is láojià, and when is it used?
Which expression would speakers from other areas of China use instead?
What do Chinese punctuation rules allow?
What is the Wángfǔjǐng Boulevard area?
Write the Chinese for "Excuse me, where is there a place to buy books?"
Give the literal rendering of the reply in exchange 2.

answers.answer_text: "On Wángfǔjǐng Boulevard there is a New China Bookstore. It is very large."

questions_and_answers.question_text: When may two sentences be separated by a comma instead of a period?

answers.answer_text: If the relationship between the sentences is considered very close.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Name two things found in the Wángfǔjǐng Boulevard area.

answers.answer_text: Bǎihuò Dàlóu (a state-owned department store) and Dōngfēng Shìchǎng (a large enclosed market) — as well as bookstores, antique shops, and hotels.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Which dialect does láojià belong to?
Write the Chinese for "There is a New China Bookstore on Wángfǔjǐng Boulevard that is very large."

answers.answer_text: Wángfǔjǐng Dàjiē yǒu yíge Xīnhuá Shūdiàn, hěn dà.

articles.text:
2. A: Láojià, nǎr yǒu mài shūde?     Excuse me, where is there a place
                                      to buy books?
   C: Wángfǔjǐng Dàjiē yǒu yíge      There is a New China Bookstore on
      Xīnhuá Shūdiàn, hěn dà.        Wángfǔjǐng Boulevard that is
                                      very large.

Notes on No. 2

Láojià is a Běijīng expression used when asking a person to do something. In exchange 2, a person is being asked to give directions. Speakers of Chinese from other areas of China would probably use qǐngwèn.

Hěn dà, "(It is) very big": Notice that in the English translation two Chinese sentences have been combined. Literally, the Chinese means "On Wángfǔjǐng Boulevard there is a New China Bookstore. It is very large." Chinese punctuation rules allow two sentences to be separated by a comma instead of a period if the relationship between the sentences is considered very close.

Wángfǔjǐng Dàjiē: The Wángfǔjǐng Boulevard area is a major shopping district in Běijīng. Bǎihuò Dàlóu (a state-owned department store), Dōngfēng Shìchǎng (a large enclosed market), bookstores, antique shops, and hotels are found there.
